title: The Water That Went Uphill
premise: At a desert caravan rest house, forty litres have vanished from the sealed drinking reserve. The three residents agree that nobody entered or left last night. The well is dry until the next delivery. Establish who took the water, how, and for what purpose before the departing caravan is searched. Iman says she heard nothing all night, although the roof tank gauge has risen. She alone controls tomorrow's water sales and has already refused an extra allotment.

places.name: Central Court
places.description: An awning shades empty benches. Three corridors and a stair meet beside the drinking station.

places.name: Accounts Room
places.description: Shelves of route books face a desk with a sand timer.

places.name: Roof Terrace
places.description: The horizon shimmers beyond a parapet. A maintenance ladder leads down into the court.

places.name: Supply Room
places.description: Spare fittings sit in neat compartments beside the reserve tank.

places.name: Sheltered Yard
places.description: Old transport crates shelter a row of covered animal pens.

characters.name: Iman Rook
characters.persona: She regards every traveller as a temporary responsibility, but depends on tomorrow's sales to balance her books. She snaps her folding purse shut when irritated.
characters.speech_style: Brusque practical questions, impatient fragments, reluctant affectionate terms for travellers.
characters.fallback_line: Sit in the shade while you sort that out, dear.

characters.name: Nuri Bell
characters.persona: He says he spent the evening settling his animals and repairing equipment for departure. He knots and unknots the cord on his canvas hat when pressed.
characters.speech_style: Gentle understatement, long pauses before personal matters.
characters.fallback_line: There is always something to mend before a journey.

characters.name: Vera Holt
characters.persona: She surveys routes and keeps the rest house telegraph book between journeys. She distrusts accusations based on temperament and aligns her surveying pencils before answering.
characters.speech_style: Conditional statements resolved into crisp conclusions.
characters.fallback_line: A possibility is not yet an explanation.

clues.text: The metered draw was forty litres at 22:14. A resident's service token operated the outlet; the mechanism records no individual number. The manager's master key did not turn.
A siphon hose in the Supply Room has been spliced; its cut end fits the missing end of Nuri Bell's animal-watering tube, including a crescent nick. The bypass socket is narrower than a bucket handle.
Nuri Bell received a veterinary telegram prescribing forty litres overnight for dehydrated confiscated tortoises. His transport allotment was exhausted, and he had been refused an emergency advance.
In the gravity test, water poured into the roof pipe emerges inside the reserve. The pipe rises three metres above the reserve outlet. The equipment inventory lists buckets and tubing, but no pump.
Undisturbed dust covers the perimeter path, with no wheel ruts or footprints crossing it. The outer gate bolt still carries yesterday's unbroken paper seal.
The graduated basins beside the animal pens contain thirty litres. The bedding weighs ten kilograms more than the unused dry batch; both were weighed in identical trays.
The outlet service record specifies that the bypass whistles when open. During the kitchen fan's timed run from 22:10 to 22:20, a test whistle cannot be heard from the sleeping rooms.

Iman saw Nuri Bell through the courtyard window at 22:14, carrying a coil. His wrist band was still riveted shut around his personal brass disc; hers lay in the locked cash drawer and Vera's was sealed there overnight too.
The night porter's signed watch sheet, left before his dawn departure, records Iman counting receipts behind the office grille continuously from 22:00 to 22:30. The only exit passes his chair.
Nuri Bell admits he drew the ration into his treatment troughs after permission was refused. He says he could not watch the confiscated tortoises die while waiting for morning.

solution.motive: Keep confiscated tortoises alive after an emergency water request was refused.
solution.method: Use his wrist token and a spliced narrow siphon through the reserve outlet bypass while the kitchen fan masked the sound.
true_timeline: 18:00 The courier receives the treatment instruction and requests an advance.
19:00 The manager refuses because the reserve is allocated to departing travellers.
22:10 The kitchen fan starts its timed cycle.
22:14 Nuri operates the outlet with his wrist token and siphons forty litres.
22:20 The fan stops; the water is already in the animal basins and bedding.
08:00 The remaining reserve still covers the departing caravan's drinking allocation; the theft has consumed the emergency margin.
